introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.
enonce_intro_markdown: A particle of mass $m$ is projected vertically downward from a great height with speed $\dfrac{g}{3k}$ in a medium whose resistance to motion is $mkv$, where $v$ is the speed at time $t$ and $k$ is a constant. The speed doubles after time $T$ when the particle has fallen a distance $X$.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Take downward as positive. Newton's second law:

$$m\frac{dv}{dt}=mg-mkv\ \Longrightarrow\ \frac{dv}{dt}=g-kv=k\left(\frac gk-v\right).$$

Separate the variables, with $v$ going from $\dfrac{g}{3k}$ to $\dfrac{2g}{3k}$ while $t$ goes from $0$ to $T$:

$$\int_{g/(3k)}^{2g/(3k)}\frac{dv}{g-kv}=\int_0^T dt\ \Longrightarrow\ \left[-\frac1k\ln(g-kv)\right]_{g/(3k)}^{2g/(3k)}=T.$$

At the limits, $g-kv=g-\dfrac{g}{3}=\dfrac{2g}{3}$ (lower) and $g-kv=g-\dfrac{2g}{3}=\dfrac{g}{3}$ (upper):

$$T=-\frac1k\left[\ln\frac g3-\ln\frac{2g}{3}\right]=\frac1k\ln\frac{2g/3}{g/3}=\frac{\ln 2}{k}.$$

Hence $kT=\ln 2$. $\blacksquare$

Use $a=v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$ with $x$ measured downward from the point of projection:

$$v\frac{dv}{dx}=g-kv\ \Longrightarrow\ \frac{dx}{dv}=\frac{v}{g-kv}.$$

Write $\dfrac{v}{g-kv}=-\dfrac1k+\dfrac{g/k}{g-kv}$ (check: $-\dfrac{g-kv}{k(g-kv)}+\dfrac{g}{k(g-kv)}=\dfrac{kv}{k(g-kv)}$). Then

$$X=\int_{g/(3k)}^{2g/(3k)}\left[-\frac1k+\frac{g}{k}\cdot\frac{1}{g-kv}\right]dv=\left[-\frac vk-\frac{g}{k^2}\ln(g-kv)\right]_{g/(3k)}^{2g/(3k)}.$$

Evaluate the two parts:

$$-\frac1k\left(\frac{2g}{3k}-\frac{g}{3k}\right)=-\frac{g}{3k^2},$$

$$-\frac{g}{k^2}\left[\ln\frac g3-\ln\frac{2g}{3}\right]=\frac{g}{k^2}\ln2.$$

Therefore

$$X=\frac{g}{k^2}\left(\ln2-\frac13\right)\ \Longrightarrow\ k^2X=g\left(\ln2-\frac13\right).\ \blacksquare$$
